summary:
Telemetry batch identities are built as `<invocation>-%06d<sequence>` (ObservedCodexProcess.fs, ingestId). The leading invocation token is a per-run generation, so it identifies one agent run, not a producer association. Observed case (UTEL-H3, issue #4516 comments 6343114421 and 6342965141, investigated read-only from file metadata and source on 2026-10-22): invocation `002ca0e2c0af4d2f9bebcaf30536a40a` was a single terminal agent run with 3 applied receipts on 2026-10-03. Sequence numbering ended at 3 with the run, so no genuine ordinal 4 exists or can exist; sending one would be fabrication. Do not treat such an ID as an association to resume, repoint or clone.

The canonical persistent association for workspace `utel-home-20261003` is the passive producer `codex-passive-home-01`, stream `native-usage`, credential reference `home-passive-programme-v1`. The client engine derives the credential environment variable from the reference by upper-casing and replacing `-` with `_`, here FSGG_TELEMETRY_CREDENTIAL_HOME_PASSIVE_PROGRAMME_V1 (WorkspaceTelemetryApplication.fs, credential). The receiver authorizes by exact producer, stream and workspace scope (TelemetryReceipt.authorize), so a credential for a different producer refuses these batches and relabelling them would be forbidden repointing. Custody of the secret stays with Home (#4705); it never appears in an issue, argument or this record.

Hold ownership: an "ordinal 4 overflow / last-claim" hold belongs to process-supervision `process_resume` (FS.GG.Coordination#1026), not to telemetry, and does not apply to these batches. The holds that do apply come from #4638: no repointing, cloning or rewriting of queued state, and the retained Unknown reservations stay retained.

Limits: this is an observation dated 2026-10-22 from the cited issue comment and the cited source at the stated revision; association and enrollment state are live facts. Refresh them from the producer config and the receiver before action. The record grants no enrollment, send or drain authority.
title: A UTEL batch-ID prefix names one finished run, not a persistent association
